items.title: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek
items.summary: As we get closer to the release date for Kubernetes v1.38, the project develops and matures,features may be deprecated, removed, or replaced with better ones for the project's overall health.This blog post outlines some of the planned changes for the Kubernetes v1.38 release that therelease team feels you should be aware of for the continued maintenance of your Kubernetesenvironment and keeping up to date with the latest changes. The information listed below is basedon the current status of the v1.38 release and may change before the actual release date.Deprecations and removals for Kubernetes v1.38kubectl: WebSocket opt-out environment variables removedkubectl has used WebSockets instead of SPDY by default for kubectl exec, attach and cp sincev1.30, and for kubectl port-forward since v1.31. The KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS andKUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS environment variables let you turn that behavior off. Thesevariables are going to be removed in v1.38. kubectl will then always try WebSockets first and fallback to SPDY when it needs to (the same as the current default behavior). If your scripts or CIenvironments set either of these environment variables, you can remove them since they will nolonger have any effect.To learn more, refer toKEP-4006: Transition from SPDY to WebSockets.kubectl: name dropped from kuberc credential plugin allowlist entriesThe kuberc file keeps kubectl user preferences separate from cluster credentials in thekubeconfig, including an allowlist of the credential plugins kubectl is allowed to run. In thebeta kubectl.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 API, an allowlist entry can use name as an alias forcommand. The name field (not command) has been deprecated since v1.36.With kuberc expected to graduate to stable in v1.38, the new kubectl.config.k8s.io/v1 API willnot include name. If any of your allowlist entries use name, change them to command now.To learn more, refer toKEP-3104: Separate kubectl user preferences from cluster configs.Ongoing major changesFuture removal of cgroup v1 supportSupport for cgroup v1 is being phased out. Since v1.35, the kubelet fails to start on nodes that usecgroup v1 unless you set failCgroupV1: false in the kubelet configuration. This option remainsavailable in v1.38, but it should be treated as a short-term fix as support for cgroup v1 is plannedto be removed in a future release. If you haven't already, please plan your migration tocgroup v2.To learn more, refer toKEP-5573: Remove cgroup v1 support.Admission webhooks no longer receive authentication and authorization review requestsSince v1.37, the ExcludeAdmissionWebhookVirtualResources feature gate has been enabled by default.With it on, validating and mutating admission webhooks no longer receive requests for (virtual)writes to TokenReview, SelfSubjectReview, SubjectAccessReview, SelfSubjectAccessReview,LocalSubjectAccessReview or SelfSubjectRulesReview. Creating or updating a webhook configurationwhose rules name one of these resources returns a deprecation warning, and the API server logs anyexisting configurations that are affected when it starts.If you rely on a webhook to see these requests, you can turn the feature gate off for now, but notethat the gate is planned to be locked on when the feature graduates to stable.To learn more, refer toKEP-5793: Manifest Based Admission Control Config.Breaking changes in Kubernetes v1.38Container runtimes must report the cgroup driverThe kubelet in v1.37 and older supported releases provides a legacy mechanism to configure thecgroup driver. The modern way to do that is via the CRI RuntimeConfig RPC, which reports thecgroup driver that the container runtime recommends using. In v1.38, the kubelet defaults to notallowing the legacy configuration mechanism: it will be both deprecated and unavailable unlessexplicitly re-activated. As a result, v1.38 nodes will essentially require that your containerruntime is running before the kubelet starts (to look up the expected cgroup driver); if thekubelet can't get the cgroup driver from the runtime even after retrying, it will exit with an errorbefore even registering the node.As part of this upcoming release, the cgroupDriver field in the kubelet configuration file will bedeprecated. Not only is specifying that field going to be deprecated, the kubelet will actuallyreject it unless you reactivate the legacy mechanism by enabling the (temporary)LegacyCgroupDriverFallback feature gate. The kubeadm tool will also no longer set cgroupDriverto systemd by default, and its preflight checks will report an error if the runtime doesn'tsupport the RPC. If any of your nodes run an older, incompatible container runtime, you shouldfollow the instructions in the official v1.38 release notes about how to upgrade.To learn more, refer toKEP-4033: Discover cgroup driver from CRI andkubernetes/kubernetes#136731.Pod-level resources: swap behavior changes on LimitedSwap nodesIf you use pod-level resources on Linux nodes that use cgroup v2 a
